title: A ReLU at the fixpipe feeding an L0C accumulator back into L1
surface: Tensor.relu() on an L0C accumulator stored directly into an FP16 L1 tile; SEvent(Pipe.FIX, Pipe.MTE1) set and waited explicitly inside auto_sync(); two matmul calls in one kernel(mode="cube") launch, the second consuming the first's result
study_for: The feedback path is the subject: an FP32 L0C accumulator becomes an FP16 L1 tile through `l0c_mid.relu()` and is consumed by the next `matmul` in the same launch, without passing through UB or GM. The conversion, the clamp and the store are one fixpipe operation.

`SEvent(Pipe.FIX, Pipe.MTE1)` is set and waited by hand even though the body runs inside `auto_sync()`. Those are the two pipes actually involved -- the fixpipe writes the L1 tile and MTE1 reads it back for the second product -- and naming them is what orders the two.

One cell of the output is the ReLU witness, and it was planted. `x[0]` is all ones and `y[1]` all minus ones, so the intermediate at (0, 1) is -32 before the clamp; `z[0]` is zero except `z[0, 1] = 1`, which reads that single cell into `output[0, 0]`. A kernel that dropped the clamp prints -32 there instead of 0, and `compare` prints that cell on every run. Without the planted rows a random signed input might clamp nothing at all.

The bitwise comparison is earned rather than assumed. Operands are integers in [-3, 3], so the first product is at most 288 in magnitude -- exactly representable in FP16 -- and the second product is exact in FP32. `check_domain` asserts the domain that makes each of those true, so widening the operands fails the assertion instead of silently making the comparison wrong.

The reference computes both products in integer arithmetic and clamps with `clamp_min(0)`. It calls no fixpipe helper, no conversion helper and nothing from the kernel, so agreement is evidence about the device rather than about the library agreeing with itself.
do_not_copy_when: Your intermediate can exceed the FP16 exact-integer range. The whole comparison rests on the feedback boundary being exact for this domain; past 2048 it is not, and you need a tolerance and a different reference.
Your operands are not integral. Nothing here establishes how arbitrary FP16 values round at the fixpipe conversion, and no exceptional value -- infinity, NaN, subnormal -- appears in this domain.
You are relying on auto_sync() alone to order a fixpipe write against an MTE1 read. This kernel names the event explicitly; treat that as part of the pattern, not as decoration.
Your tiles are not complete. M=N=P=16 and K=32 are fixed here, and no tail, padding or multi-core split is exercised -- a second core would need its own ownership statement.
